hindi: साहस सम्बन्धियों वाला बलपूर्वक कर्म है।
notes: Verbless; the copula is supplied. anvayavat (from anvaya, 'lineage, kin') is read literally as 'having kin'; it may be an adverb or a neuter adjective, and the text does not say whose kin; no further sense is imported. sāhasa = rashness (glossary 12.2). karma = action.

hindi: सम्बन्धियों से रहित में चोरी है, और हटा ले जाने में।
english: In [the case of one] without kin, [it is] theft; and in carrying off.
notes: Verbless; the copula is supplied only as a bare copula. apavyayana (apa-vi-ayana) is obscure and is rendered literally as 'carrying off'; alternatives such as 'removal' or 'squandering' are possible. What 'niranvaye' qualifies is not stated (a person, or a case); kept as 'without kin'. The sentence is incomplete: the second item has no predicate in the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: of gems, valuables, worthless goods, raw materials

hindi: “रत्न, बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं, तुच्छ वस्तुओं, कुप्य के साहस में दण्ड मूल्य के समान है”, ऐसा मानव कहते हैं।
english: “In rashness concerning gems, valuables, worthless goods and raw materials, the penalty [is] equal to the value,” say the Manavas.
notes: sāra = valuables (glossary 12.1), kupya = raw materials; phalgu 'worthless' (literally 'insignificant, weak'). daṇḍa beside a value = penalty. The closing iti is carried by the quotation marks.

hindi: “मूल्य का दुगुना”, ऐसा औशनस कहते हैं।
english: “[The penalty is] twice the value,” say the Aushanasas.
notes: The predicate (daṇḍaḥ of unit 3) is understood and bracketed in English only. Aushanasas = the followers of Ushanas (glossary 3.6).

hindi: “अपराध के अनुसार”, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।

text_flags.why: possible missing final ṃ: an avyayībhāva compound ends in -m; the printed form ends in -a
closing iti with no opening quotation mark in the unit (compare units 3 and 4); the view is quoted in the translation

notes: The predicate (the penalty) is understood and not supplied. Compare glossary 3.8.6 for a closing iti with no opening quote.

words.gloss: flowers, fruits, vegetables, roots, tubers, cooked food, hides, bamboo, clay wares
words.gram: dvandva, first member of a compound with ādīnām

hindi: “फूल, फल, शाक, मूल, कन्द, पका अन्न, चर्म, बाँस, मिट्टी का माल आदि छोटी वस्तुओं के लिए बारह पण या उससे कम, चौबीस पण या उससे अधिक दण्ड है।
english: “For petty goods—flowers, fruits, vegetables, roots, tubers, cooked food, hides, bamboo, clay wares and so on—the penalty [is] of twelve paṇas or lower, of twenty-four paṇas or higher.

text_flags.why: stray '.-' at the end of the token before a space; the compound continues into ādīnāṃ (so the join is a compound dot, not a hyphen between words)

text_flags.suggest: (closing quote at the end of unit 10)
text_flags.why: opening quotation mark never closed in this unit; the quotation of the teachers runs through units 6 to 10 and closes in unit 10

notes: The quotation opened here closes in unit 10; the English and Hindi quote marks follow the printed quote. The first token is a compound that continues in the next token (ādīnām), so ādīnām has its own entry. The glossary (4.10) renders X-paṇa-avara as 'of X paṇas or lower'; read as a range the sense is plainly 'from twelve paṇas up to twenty-four paṇas' (avara 'lower', para 'higher' limit; see unit 30 of ch01). Alternatives: 'at least/at most'. paṇa is a unit name. bhāṇḍa = wares (glossary 4.6); mṛd-bhāṇḍa 'clay wares' (alternatively 'clay and wares'). kṣudraka = petty; pakva-anna = cooked food.

words.gloss: of black iron, wood, rope goods, small animals, cloth and so on

hindi: काला लोहा, लकड़ी, रस्सी की वस्तुएँ, छोटे पशु, वस्त्र आदि मोटी वस्तुओं के लिए चौबीस पण या उससे कम, अड़तालीस पण या उससे अधिक दण्ड है।
english: For coarse goods—black iron, wood, rope goods, small animals, cloth and so on—the penalty [is] of twenty-four paṇas or lower, of forty-eight paṇas or higher.
notes: Continues the quotation of unit 6. Same avara/para note as unit 6 (range 24 to 48 paṇas). kāla-āyasa read literally as 'black iron'; rajju-dravya 'rope goods' and the division of the list (e.g. kṣudra-paśu 'small animals') are uncertain. sthūlaka = coarse (glossary 4.1).

words.gloss: of copper, vṛtta, bell-metal, glass, tooth wares and so on

hindi: ताँबे, वृत्त, काँसे, काँच, दाँत के माल आदि मोटी वस्तुओं के लिए अड़तालीस पण या उससे कम, छियानवे या उससे अधिक प्रथम साहस-दण्ड है।
english: For coarse goods—copper, vṛtta, bell-metal, glass, tooth wares and so on—[the penalty is] the first fine for rashness, of forty-eight paṇas or lower, of ninety-six or higher.
notes: Continues the quotation of unit 6. vṛtta is obscure and kept untranslated (glossary 5.2). danta 'tooth' is literal ('ivory' possible). kaṃsa 'bell-metal' (alternatively 'brass'). ṣaṇ.ṇavati is the regular sandhi of ṣaṭ-navati. The range reads 48 to 96. pūrva-sāhasa-daṇḍa = the first fine for rashness (glossary 3.8); the middle and highest fines follow in units 9 and 10.

words.gloss: of large animals, men, fields, houses, money, gold, fine cloth and so on

hindi: बड़े पशु, मनुष्य, खेत, घर, धन, सोना, बारीक वस्त्र आदि मोटी वस्तुओं के लिए दो सौ या उससे कम, पाँच सौ या उससे अधिक मध्यम साहस-दण्ड है।
english: For coarse goods—large animals, men, fields, houses, money, gold, fine cloth and so on—[the penalty is] the middle fine for rashness, of two hundred or lower, of five hundred or higher.
notes: Continues the quotation of unit 6. hiraṇya = money (glossary 5.2; 'gold' only here in notes) beside suvarṇa = gold. Units of the figures are not stated (none added). The range reads 200 to 500. manuṣya 'men' (human beings) as printed.

words.gram: caus. pres. part. √bandh, m. gen. sg.
caus. pres. part. √muc, m. gen. sg.

hindi: स्त्री या पुरुष को दबाकर बाँधने वाले, बँधवाने वाले या बन्धन छुड़वाने वाले के लिए पाँच सौ या उससे कम, हज़ार या उससे अधिक सर्वोच्च साहस-दण्ड है”, ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: For one who, having overpowered a woman or a man, binds, or causes to bind, or causes a bond to be released—[the penalty is] the highest fine for rashness, of five hundred or lower, of a thousand or higher,” say the teachers.

text_flags.why: stray stop bar '|' before the closing quotation mark (no other unit of the chapter has one); the quotation opened in unit 6 closes here, so the mark is unopened within this unit

notes: Closes the quotation opened in unit 6 (units 6 to 10 are one passage of the teachers). Without the bar the sentence is the same. 'bandhaṃ mokṣayataḥ' is read literally as 'causing a bond to be released'; who is released is not stated (alternative: one who frees a bound person). The genitives (badhnataḥ, bandhayataḥ, mokṣayataḥ) are read as 'for one who ...'. Range 500 to 1000.

hindi: “जो ‘स्वीकार करने वाला’ के रूप में साहस करवाता है, वह दुगुना दे।
english: “Whoever causes rashness to be done [as] ‘the one who accepts’, he should give double.

text_flags.why: opening quotation mark not closed in this unit; the quotation of the Barhaspatyas runs through units 11 to 13 and closes in unit 13

notes: pratipattṛ (prati-√pad) obscure here: 'one who accepts / undertakes' (cf. glossary pratipanna); whose acceptance is meant is not said. Mid-line iti is shown by the quotation marks (4.4 pattern). The object of dadyāt is not stated (a penalty is understood); nothing is supplied. The quotation opened here runs on to unit 13; the inner quotation 'pratipattā' is printed with plain marks too.

hindi: ‘जितना धन काम में लाया जाएगा, उतना मैं दूँगा’ — वह चौगुना दण्ड दे।
english: ‘As much money as will be used, so much I will give’—he should give a fourfold penalty.

text_flags.why: possible: the junction d + h is written ddh (yāvad dhiraṇyam), and the space has fallen inside the junction; as printed yāvadd carries a stray d

notes: Continues the quotation of the Barhaspatyas opened in unit 11, so the inner words are in single quotes in the translation. upayokṣyate is read as future passive of upa-√yuj ('will be used'); the e-text may also intend a middle form with the same sense. daṇḍam = penalty (glossary 4). The speaker of the quoted words is the one who has the act done; not stated.

hindi: जो ‘मैं इतना धन दूँगा’ इस रूप में परिमाण निर्दिष्ट करके करवाता है, वह कहे अनुसार धन और दण्ड दे”, ऐसा बार्हस्पत्य कहते हैं।
english: Whoever, having specified the measure [as] ‘I will give this much money’, causes [it] to be done, he should give the money as stated and the penalty,” say the Barhaspatyas.

text_flags.why: possible: the junction d + h is written ddh (etāvad dhiraṇyaṃ), and the space has fallen inside the junction; as printed etāvadd carries a stray d
closing quotation mark with no opening mark in this unit; the quotation opened in unit 11 closes here

notes: Closes the quotation of the Barhaspatyas opened in unit 11. The object of kārayati (rashness) is understood, bracketed in English only. 'iti pramāṇam uddiśya' is read as specifying the amount in the quoted words. yathā-uktam 'as stated' refers back to the stated sum.

hindi: “यदि वह क्रोध, मद या मोह का बहाना बताए, तो इस पर कहे अनुसार दण्ड लगाए”, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “If he should allege anger, intoxication or delusion, [one] should impose on him the penalty as stated,” says Kautilya.

text_flags.why: closing iti with no opening quotation mark in the unit; the view is quoted in the translation

notes: kopa = anger (glossary 8.3). apadiś 'allege as a pretext' (literally 'point to'). The subject of kuryāt is not stated, so '[one]' as in glossary 4.9. enam is read as 'him'; it may agree with daṇḍam ('this penalty'). The closing iti is carried by quotation marks (glossary 3.8.6).

hindi: सब दण्ड-कर्मों में रूप आठ पण सौ पर; सौ से परे वालों में व्याजी को पाँच पण सौ पर जानना चाहिए।
english: In all penalty-actions the rūpa [is] eight paṇas [per] hundred; among [those] beyond a hundred, one should know the vyājī [as] five paṇas [per] hundred.
notes: rūpa and vyājī are kept as technical terms (glossary 4.1: rūpa also 'coin'; vyājī not Hindi 'interest'); their sense (a charge or rate on fines) is not stated. 'per' is supplied from the structure 'eight paṇas, a hundred'. 'pareṣu' (loc. pl.) 'among [those] beyond' is uncertain; the ablative śatāt 'than a hundred' depends on para. ca is rendered 'and' (vyājī joined to what is known). daṇḍa-karman = action of penalty (glossary 4.10).

hindi: प्रजाओं के दोषों की अधिकता से या राजाओं के भाव-दोष से रूप और व्याजी अत्यन्त अधर्मपूर्ण हैं, किन्तु प्रकृति धर्मसंगत मानी गई है।
english: From the abundance of faults of the people, or from fault of disposition of kings, rūpa and vyājī [are] very unrighteous; but nature is remembered [as] righteous.
notes: Obscure verse; confidence low. adharmiṣṭhe is read as a dual neuter predicate agreeing with rūpa-vyājyau; it could also be a locative singular ('in the very unrighteous [case]'), which would give 'rūpa and vyājī [apply] in the very unrighteous [case]'. prakṛti is read as 'nature' (the natural or normal state), contrasted with the two charges; other senses ('natural rate', 'constituent element') are possible. 'smṛtā' is rendered 'remembered' (i.e. held in tradition). rūpa and vyājī as in unit 15.
